description: The signed Master-to-peer contract for the peer's OpenShell execution sandbox. A request may inspect, create, start, stop or delete a sandbox and read or change its policy; it never reads vault content and never widens a mount. The peer executes the verified action against its own gateway with its own local credentials.
implementation: The signed envelope and verification grammar are implemented. The bridge `/sandbox/*` route and the signed executor are not implemented; the capability is inert (peer PLAN 20E).

request.signature: Ed25519 over canonical JSON of signed_fields. It records who asked; the capability is read only from the peer's signed registry entry.

list.rule: Return the gateway inventory. The response names sandboxes and states, never mounted host paths or policy bodies.

get.rule: Return one sandbox record and its resolved workload identity; no host path and no credential is returned.

create.rule: Create a sandbox from the image with the signed policy and the signed mount list. The peer refuses an image or mount outside its local whitelist.

start.rule: Start an existing sandbox under its stored policy; no new mount may appear.

stop.rule: Stop a sandbox; the record and its persistent mounts remain.

delete.rule: Delete a sandbox record and its compute resource. A persistent bind mount is never deleted with it.

policy-get.rule: Return the active policy. It may name paths, not file contents.

policy-update.rule: Apply the signed policy. Network rules may change live; filesystem, Landlock and process changes require sandbox recreation and are refused rather than applied to a running sandbox.

expose.rule: Expose one sandbox-local TCP port through an authenticated gateway forward. The peer refuses a port it did not create and never exposes a host path.

identity.model: The workload runs with the node owner's Unix identity, resolved on the peer at creation time. The peer chooses the driver; a sandbox request does not.

docker-rootful.identity: Numeric owner UID/GID; run_as_user and run_as_group are the numeric selectors.
docker-rootful.status: blocked on the current Jetson pair until Docker 28+ and Landlock ABI 3 are available.

vm.identity: The symbolic sandbox guest account, reconciled by the driver to sandbox_uid/sandbox_gid; those must equal the node owner.
vm.status: validated on a supported host; blocked on the current Jetson pair because the embedded libkrun requires GLIBC 2.33.

identity.supplementary_groups: A numeric selector skips initgroups, so a Docker sandbox receives only the primary GID. It must never inherit docker, sudo or equivalent host groups. A VM sandbox uses the reconciled guest account with the owner's primary GID.
identity.mount_scope: One read-write bind per sandbox (the user's peer-<id> vault). A VM sandbox also has one read-only mount for its generated OpenCode config directory. Isolation between users is mount-scoped, not UID-scoped, because they share the node owner's Unix account.
identity.excluded_driver_reason: Rootless Podman maps the container uid through an unpinned subuid range, not to the host user (OpenShell issue 2336), and the driver exposes no userns/keep-id setting; it is excluded until that changes.

policy.filesystem: read_only and read_write lists are absolute, at most 256 paths, and read_write cannot contain /.
policy.landlock: hard_requirement protects container-internal paths only; the kernel needs Landlock ABI v3 or later.
policy.bind_mounts: Bind-mounted paths bypass filesystem_policy (OpenShell issue 1748, closed as not planned). The mount's read_only flag is the boundary; the policy must still declare the same paths so intent and mount agree.
policy.network: The workload has no network interface. Egress is the supervisor's policy; loopback, link-local and 169.254.169.254 are never reachable.
policy.approvals: OpenShell proposal auto-approval stays off. A policy proposal is surfaced to the local user; the Master cannot approve on the user's behalf.

rules: Authority comes from the Master signature plus sandbox-supervise in the peer's registry; neither alone executes.
The peer keeps the gateway credential. The Master never receives a token, a host socket or a shell.
A sandbox-request is authority, never knowledge: it cannot carry a vault page, an answer or a prompt.
The peer's local execution whitelist is narrower than this contract and can refuse an otherwise valid request.
A mount may only name a path the peer itself provisioned for that user; no $HOME, .state, key, sibling vault or Docker socket.
Unsigned, stale, replayed or unknown-capability requests are refused before any gateway call.
